chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: People say that forgiveness descends upon the one who fasts the month of Ramadan on Laylat al-Qadr. So he said: “O Ḥasan, the worker is only given his wage upon completing his work, and likewise the servant.”
I said: Then what should we do in it? He said: “When the sun sets, perform ghusl, and when you have prayed the three rakʿahs, raise your hand and say...” The rest of the hadith.

The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The ghusl for entering the city of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to perform an obligatory act therein or a recommended one is sunnah (recommended); the ghusl for entering Makkah for the like of that is sunnah; the ghusl for visiting the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is sunnah; the ghusl for visiting the graves of the Imams عليهم السلام is sunnah; the ghusl for entering the Kaʿbah is sunnah; the ghusl for entering al-Masjid al-Ḥarām is sunnah; and the ghusl of mubāhalah is sunnah.

These ghusls have already been mentioned in the hadith of ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā from Samāʿah, and some of them in the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Muslim mentioned earlier, and in those two there is sufficiency from citing other than them, if Allah Most High wills. The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The ghusl of repentance from major sins is sunnah.

key_terms.الْمَغْفِرَةَ: forgiveness from Allah granted to His servants
key_terms.الْمُبَاهَلَةِ: the ritual act of mutual invocation for divine judgment
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ: visiting, especially a sacred grave or shrine
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree in Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What ghusls are recommended in Shia hadith for Laylat al-Qadr, sacred visits, and repentance?
ai.summary: This report mentions recommended acts connected to Laylat al-Qadr, especially ghusl and du'a after prayer, and compares divine reward to a worker receiving wages upon completing his task. It also records several recommended ghusls related to sacred places, ziyārah, mubāhalah, and repentance from major sins.
